turns.doctor_question: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Well, I... I mean, I'm here because my husband insisted, but really, I’m the one who’s been trying to get people to pay attention. For months now—honestly, it’s been going on since at least the spring, maybe earlier if I really sit down and map it out—but for months I’ve been trying to get people to understand that my husband’s family is quietly messing with our money. And not just our money, our good name, too. 

They are very subtle about it, which is why it’s so frustrating when no one believes me. I work as a billing clerk, so I know numbers, I know when things don't add up. And these... these little billing errors keep showing up at my work. Just tiny discrepancies. Most people would just write it off as a glitch in the system or a typo, but I know what I'm looking at. I do this for a living. 

And it’s not just at the office, it’s bleeding into everything else. Like at church, suddenly people I’ve sat next to for years are acting funny toward me, whispering, avoiding eye contact during fellowship hour. It’s because of the things his family is saying and doing behind the scenes. And the most aggravating part is that people will say, "Oh, let's just look at the paperwork, let's check the accounts," but no matter what records anyone pulls up—work logs, bank statements, whatever—they've covered their tracks so well that it looks normal to anyone else. But I know it ties back to them. I can see the pattern, and it’s just exhausting trying to get someone to actually see what they are doing to us.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses a fixed, persecutory belief that her husband's family is sabotaging her finances and reputation, maintaining this conviction even when objective records contradict her claims.

top_partial.disease_name: Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever heard voices, whispering, or other sounds when no one was around or when others couldn't hear them?
turns.patient_response: No, no, I don't hear anything like that. I mean, I'm not crazy. I know people probably think I am, especially my husband when I try to show him the discrepancies in the billing logs, but I don't hear voices. The whispering I mentioned at church, that's real whispering. Like, I can see them leaning into each other, Mary and Susan specifically, just last Sunday during the coffee hour. They leaned in, covered their mouths a bit, and I know they were talking about the rumors his family started. But it's actual people, right there in the room, saying things under their breath. It's not like I'm sitting in an empty room hearing things that aren't there. I'm very grounded in reality, which is why I can see the pattern in the numbers at work when everyone else is just blindly trusting the system. I rely on facts, on what I can see and prove, even if they've made it nearly impossible to prove to anyone else. So, no, no imaginary voices or sounds. Just the very real, very frustrating reality of what his family is doing.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient describes fixed beliefs about people whispering about rumors started by her husband's family and seeing hidden patterns in billing logs that others cannot see, indicating persecutory and referential delusions.
symptom_reasoning.S020: The patient explicitly denies hearing imaginary voices or sounds when no one is around.

turns.doctor_question: Aside from feeling frustrated about this situation, how has your mood been—have you felt persistently down, depressed, or hopeless?
turns.patient_response:
Depressed? No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, who even has the time to be depressed with all this going on? If I were hopeless, I would have just thrown my hands up and let them ruin us by now, right? I would have just let them take the money and destroy my reputation. But I haven't. I'm fighting it. 

I get up every single morning at 6 AM sharp, I make my coffee—usually just instant lately because I really don't have the patience to wait for the drip machine when my mind is already racing about what I might find at work that day—and I get myself ready. I actually feel pretty energized most days, or... well, maybe keyed up is a better way to put it, but definitely not down in the dumps. I mean, sure, it’s exhausting. You try going to the office every day knowing you have to triple-check every single invoice and ledger because someone is intentionally tweaking things to make you look incompetent. It absolutely wears on a person. 

But depressed? No, no. My aunt Patricia, now she was depressed. Years ago, she wouldn't even get out of bed for weeks at a time, just laid there in the dark with the curtains drawn tight, wouldn't even answer the phone. I am the exact opposite of that. I'm up, I'm alert, I have to be. Because I know if I let my guard down for even a split second, if I just sit around feeling sorry for myself and moping, that's exactly when his family will really do some permanent damage to our accounts. So, no, I'm not depressed or hopeless at all. Just... highly motivated to get to the bottom of it, even if it feels like I'm the only one actually doing anything about it.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses persecutory delusions, believing someone is intentionally tweaking invoices to make them look incompetent and that a family is trying to ruin them.
symptom_reasoning.S058: The patient explicitly states they feel 'keyed up' rather than depressed.
symptom_reasoning.S079: The patient describes a state of hypervigilance, stating they are 'up' and 'alert' because they cannot 'let my guard down for even a split second.'
symptom_reasoning.S024: The patient explicitly denies feeling depressed or 'down in the dumps.'
symptom_reasoning.S083: The patient explicitly denies feeling hopeless, stating they are fighting the situation and are highly motivated.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been diagnosed with any physical health conditions or medical illnesses?
turns.patient_response:
No, I haven't. I mean, physically, I'm fine. I've always been pretty healthy, honestly. I don't have diabetes or high blood pressure or any of those things that people my age start getting. I just turned 47, and I know that's when a lot of folks start having to take pills for cholesterol or whatever, but my numbers have always been good. I go to my primary care doctor for my annual checkups—Dr. Miller, he's over at the clinic on 4th Street, I've been seeing him for probably... gosh, maybe eight or nine years now? Anyway, he always says my heart sounds good, my lungs are clear. 

The only thing I ever really go to the doctor for is maybe a sinus infection once a year, usually in the late fall when the weather changes. But other than that, no major medical issues. No surgeries, no chronic conditions. I try to take care of myself, you know? I walk on the treadmill in the basement when I have time, though lately, I've been spending most of my evenings going over the billing statements from work trying to find exactly where they're making those little adjustments. So I haven't been on the treadmill as much as I should. But physically, my body is perfectly healthy. It's just the stress of this whole situation with my husband's family that's taking a toll, but that's not a medical illness, that's just... well, that's just the reality of what I'm dealing with. So, no, no physical health conditions at all.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever felt like outside forces or other people were putting thoughts directly into your mind?
turns.patient_response:
Thoughts? Like, someone beaming thoughts into my head? No, no, definitely not. That sounds like something out of a science fiction movie, you know? Like those old black-and-white films where they wear tin foil hats to stop the aliens. I don't experience anything like that. My thoughts are completely my own. I mean, if someone were putting thoughts in my head, I'd probably be thinking about something much more pleasant than billing discrepancies and my in-laws, right? I'd be thinking about a vacation in Hawaii or winning the lottery. 

But no, everything I think, everything I figure out, it comes from my own brain. It comes from me looking at the evidence, sitting there at my desk with the highlighters—I use yellow for the dates that don't match up and pink for the amounts that have been altered by just a few cents—and piecing it all together myself. No one is telling me to think this, and no one is putting the ideas there. In fact, if outside forces were doing anything, they'd be trying to take thoughts *out* of my mind so I'd stop noticing what they're up to. They'd probably love it if they could just erase my memory of what the original ledger looked like before they got into the system. 

So, no, my mind is my own. It's sharp, it's focused, and it's all me. I just wish other people would use *their* minds to look at the facts I'm laying out for them instead of acting like I'm the one who's making things up. But as for outside forces... no, nothing like that at all.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient demonstrates persecutory delusions, expressing a fixed belief that others are altering ledgers and conspiring to hide their actions.
symptom_reasoning.S031: The patient explicitly states their mind is 'sharp' and 'focused', denying any diminished ability to think.
symptom_reasoning.S059: The patient describes their mind as 'focused' and details their meticulous attention to ledgers, denying any difficulty concentrating.
